gaps.sentence: The ___ (INTERVIEW) asked her some difficult questions.
gaps.hint: the person who asks the questions (-er = doer)
gaps.explanation: The interviewer asks; the interviewee answers. The suffix -er marks the doer.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The two countries signed a peace ___ (TREAT).
gaps.explanation: A peace treaty is a formal agreement; 'treatment' means medical care or the way you behave towards someone.

gaps.sentence: The hospital provides ___ care around the clock (PERSON).
gaps.hint: adjective needed before the noun 'care'; beware the word meaning 'staff'
gaps.explanation: 'Personal care' uses the adjective 'personal'; 'personnel' is a noun meaning staff.

gaps.sentence: Her ___ (PERFORM) in the final was outstanding.
gaps.explanation: After 'Her' a noun is needed: performance (-ance noun); performers are people.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: He lost his job because of his ___ (HONESTY).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — he lost his job
gaps.explanation: Losing a job implies wrongdoing, so the negative noun 'dishonesty' (dis- + honesty) is needed.
